Subject: SKU consolidation + invoice routing question

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are trying to finalize the Azure private offer and have two asks before procurement can sign: 1) Helix wants a simplified SKU map so our billing team can consume one consolidated line item instead of 5 separate SKUs; 2) we need clarity on the reseller margin handback — our distributor requires a named handback flow on the invoice so they can reconcile commission.

I've attached our draft PO and our current Azure_SKU_Mapping.xlsx so you can see how our billing team expects the rows. Can you confirm whether Redwood can present a single consolidated SKU on the invoice and whether you can accommodate a 6% reseller handback (gross) visible on invoice line details? If not, what are the alternatives?

Also, any guidance on DocuSign placement (Helix prefers the executive signature on page 2) would be helpful. Procurement is on a tight cycle; can we get these clarifications by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
James Park
VP Procurement, HelixHealth
Procurement Team <procurement@helixhealth.com>

Diego / Kim —

Short answers and recommended approach:

1) Consolidated SKU on invoice
- Ops can present a single "Helix-Azure-Private" invoice line that maps to multiple internal SKUs. We will include an internal mapping annex (not printed on the customer's PDF invoice) for rev rec. If Helix requires the internal SKU rows on their copy, that's more work and we should push for a single customer-facing line to keep billing clean.

2) Reseller handback (6%)
- We can show a separate invoice line called "Distributor Handback (6%)" that appears on the customer-facing invoice. This will be recorded as a contra-revenue / commission pass-through in our ledger.
- Tax: if the handback is paid to a distributor in the US, we need their W-9/EIN to avoid 1099 ambiguity. If paid cross-border, tax withholding rules apply — finance needs to confirm.

3) DocuSign placement
- Legal says we can move the executive signature to page 2 for this one-off. We'd prefer to keep the rest of the template identical.

Recommended next steps (for Diego to send to Helix):
- Confirm they are OK with a single customer-facing invoice line labeled "Helix-Azure-Private" and request distributor tax id + remit instructions for the handback.
- Propose a counter: 6% visible handback as separate line, final consolidated unit price is $0.068 per reserved vCPU-hour (example), with a 12-month commit. (Ben: that sample price is illustrative — if Diego wants a different number, tell me.)

I can draft a short carveout paragraph and a one-page invoice sample. Kim — please confirm rev rec mapping and whether the internal mapping annex is necessary for ASC606 audit.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace Deals, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKU consolidation + invoice routing question

James / Procurement —

Appreciate the details and the PO draft. We can accommodate both requests with the following counterproposal:

1) Consolidated invoice line: we will present a single customer-facing line item labeled "Helix-Azure-Private (consolidated)" that maps to our internal SKU set. For auditing/revenue-recognition we will include an internal mapping annex; if Helix requires the full SKU breakdown on the customer invoice we can provide a supplemental CSV, but it will not be the default PDF invoice.

2) Reseller handback: Redwood will display a separate invoice line "Distributor Handback (6% of list)". This will be processed as a pass-through to your named distributor once we receive the distributor remit instructions and tax id/EIN. If the distributor is outside the US, please confirm tax withholding rules up front so we can route correctly.

3) Pricing corridor and term: we can hold the consolidated unit price at $0.068 per reserved vCPU-hour for a 12-month commit, with a +/- 3% corridor for usage-tier adjustments. This corridor lets both sides avoid frequent PO amendments while preserving margin guardrails for your distributor. (If you prefer a flat fixed price instead of a corridor, we can propose that in the next revision.)

4) DocuSign: we can adjust the signature placement to match your preference (executive on page 2).

Next steps: please confirm the following so we can finalize the DocuSign-ready PO by Friday:
- Approval to receive the consolidated customer-facing invoice line (yes/no)
- Distributor name, remit instructions, and tax id/EIN for the 6% handback
- Confirmation of the 12-month term and whether you accept the +/- 3% corridor

I'm copying Ben and Kim to keep ops and finance in the loop. Once we have the above, we'll issue Redwood_PO_counter_v1.pdf and send the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
